name: Saints Nereus, Achilleus and Pancras
history: Three early Roman martyrs. Nereus and Achilleus were soldiers who, Pope Damasus recorded in verse, threw down their arms when they came to believe, and died for Christ. Pancras was a boy of about fourteen beheaded on the Via Aurelia, probably under Diocletian. His cult reached England early, and churches in Canterbury and London bear his name.
life: Nereus and Achilleus were buried in the catacomb of Domitilla on the Via Ardeatina, where a basilica was later built over their tomb. Pope Damasus, in the fourth century, wrote an inscription for them: they had served a tyrant’s cruel orders as soldiers, then, suddenly converted, they fled the camp, threw away their shields and weapons, and rejoiced to bear witness to Christ. A later legend linked them with Flavia Domitilla, a Christian of the imperial family. Of Pancras we know the place of his burial on the Via Aurelia and the great devotion paid him; tradition says he was an orphan from Phrygia brought to Rome by his uncle, and that he was beheaded at about fourteen. Gregory of Tours wrote that false oaths sworn at his tomb were punished. Pope Gregory the Great sent relics of Pancras to England, and a church in his honour stood in Canterbury.
prayerTo: Saints Nereus and Achilleus, you laid down your weapons for Christ; Saint Pancras, you gave your young life for Him. Pray for soldiers, for children and young people, and for all who must choose between the faith and the demands of the world. Give me courage to be faithful in small things and in great. Amen.
penance: Pray for young people who are under pressure to abandon their faith. Keep your word today in everything, however small, in honour of Pancras, patron of oaths.
meditation: They threw away their shields and rejoiced to carry the triumph of Christ. What defences would you have to lay down to follow Him more freely?
prayer: May the holy feast of Your Martyrs, Nereus, Achilleus, Domitilla and Pancras, ever comfort us, we beseech You, O Lord, and make us worthy to serve You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
